review_scope: Original marketing image and four original smoke PNGs per assigned ID; paths relative to launch/art-07. No art edited.

denmark.summary: Coherent chalk-cliff collectible in all supplied views; finish differences and stylization, no demonstrated geometry defect.
denmark.hardware: Brass corner caps and tall front clasp remain recognizable; dark stone feet are low-contrast. Pronounced dark closed seam and stepped corner transitions are visible but do not prove a mis-seated lid. Open hinge fittings and released clasp read coherently.
denmark.terrain: Green-capped white stepped cliffs, repetitive flint shoreline and rectangular turquoise inlay are present in marketing and both closed screenshots. Faceted cliffs and straight water border are intentional miniature simplifications, not broken geometry.
denmark.texture: Marketing has finer pebbled white finish, stronger metal highlights and reflective turquoise water. Runtime is flatter, cloudier white with nearly uniform water and green caps; this is a promotional finish gap, not established geometry change.
denmark.mobile_open: Both mobile states and desktop states keep full silhouette and controls in frame. Open cavity and plain underside are readable; exterior cliff/water scene turns away, not demonstrably absent.
denmark.decision: No escalation required for the supplied stylized brief; retain caveats on seam prominence and simplified terrain.
limitations: Static endpoint images only; no independent runtime, collision, hinge-axis, rear/underside or continuous-motion verification in this review. Runtime checks were reported passed in task context, not rerun here.

equatorial-guinea.summary: Consistent basalt-gray/green Bioko concept; soft terrain and streaked material remain the principal visual limitations.
equatorial-guinea.hardware: Brass corner caps, front clasp, narrow base trim and rocky feet are visible. Closed green seam is prominent; open hinges and latch have no unambiguous visible structural failure. Mobile fine trim and foot junctions are hard to resolve.
equatorial-guinea.terrain: Low green caldera-like relief and rounded canopy clusters persist across marketing and closed desktop/mobile views. Canopy can read as green pebbles; terrain is smooth/clay-like rather than detailed basalt. Small-view caldera clarity is limited.
equatorial-guinea.texture: Marketing has crisper grain and studio metal highlights. Runtime gray diagonal streaks can read as wood or brushed cladding rather than basalt; panel boundaries emphasize this ambiguity. This is material storytelling/finish, not proven UV or mesh failure.
equatorial-guinea.mobile_open: Closed terrain remains identifiable but small; open green-gray cavity and lid underside fit completely with visible controls. No gross clipping or detached part is established.
equatorial-guinea.decision: Pass with disclosed stone-versus-wood ambiguity and abstract canopy; no mechanical rejection based on stills.

gabon.summary: Woodland and winding lagoon survive the marketing-to-runtime comparison; coherent framing in both states.
gabon.hardware: Brass corner caps, front clasp, round disc without an evident keyhole, side ring and irregular stone feet are retained. Green closed seam is conspicuous; small latch components are chunky but no demonstrated misattachment.
gabon.terrain: Three branched trees with layered rounded crowns and separate green mounds accompany a winding turquoise ribbon with pale banks. Lagoon is a flat decorative inlay, not simulated water. Closed desktop and mobile retain the recognizable composition.
gabon.texture: Marketing has sharper fine grain and softer photographic highlights; runtime pale rose-tan wood is more regular/blurred and foliage faceted. These are finish/detail limitations, not evidence of changed terrain topology.
gabon.mobile_open: Whole chest, feet, raised lid and released clasp are inside both mobile and desktop frames. Open view exposes empty wood cavity and green rim while hiding the lid-top forest/lagoon on its far face.
gabon.decision: Pass for visual continuity with stylized material caveats.
gabon.inspection_note: Direct vision requests for marketing.webp returned HTTP 400 twice. Vision succeeded on the same original with full-image region [0,0,1072,976]; this covers the complete original, not a board or derivative.

guinea.summary: Three-peak Nimba miniature and warm mineral chest are visually consistent; mineral/wood ambiguity is disclosed.
guinea.hardware: Brass corner caps, front clasp, round disc, side ring and rocky feet persist. Brass is clean rather than visibly weathered. Strong green gasket gives a slightly ajar impression in closed views but does not establish mechanical failure.
guinea.terrain: Three unequal green peaks with clustered lower greenery and small gray patches are recognizable in marketing and closed desktop/mobile. Faceted ridges and repetitive rounded clusters are stylized, not demonstrated missing surfaces.
guinea.texture: Oversized cloudy pink/brown mineral mottling can resemble burl wood in marketing and runtime. Runtime finish is softer and less differentiated across outer panels, interior and underside; not an established geometry defect.
guinea.mobile_open: Closed peaks, feet and clasp fit mobile frame; open lid, cavity and projecting released latch remain uncropped. Terrain is hidden on outer lid in open views and must not be judged missing.
guinea.decision: Pass with mineral readability, clean-versus-weathered brass and conspicuous gasket caveats.

indian-ocean.summary: Ocean/ivory-atoll geometry reads coherently, but marketing blue lid versus pale gray-beige runtime top merits an explicit presentation-fidelity decision.
indian-ocean.hardware: Gold corner fittings, front clasp, separate round disc, left ring and pale irregular limestone feet persist. Open hinge region can look separated from this front angle; no detached hinge or collision is proved. Bright closed rim is conspicuous.
indian-ocean.terrain: Ivory stepped atoll arcs surround a turquoise shallow inlay; breaks are intentional channels, not automatically holes or defects. Small desktop/mobile views do not resolve all four channels equally. Reef can read as icy formations without contextual copy.
indian-ocean.texture: Marketing lid is distinctly blue; closed runtime top is much paler gray-beige, while body is brighter cyan-blue than midnight target. Flowing marbling is consistent but can look fabric-like. Treat lid color/finish discrepancy as a promotional fidelity issue, not a confirmed geometry defect.
indian-ocean.mobile_open: Both states fit mobile and desktop framing. Open plain teal underside contrasts with patterned body; tiny pale interior strip is visible but cannot be diagnosed as penetration from these views. Exterior atoll is turned away, not proven absent.
indian-ocean.decision: Owner should decide whether the visible marketing/runtime lid-color gap is acceptable as lighting/material variation or needs presentation alignment. Do not reject on hidden hinges, released latch, irregular feet or intentional reef gaps alone.
